data.one_liner: A Flutter plugin to handle gamepad and joystick input across multiple platforms.
data.what_it_does: Handles connected gamepads, tracking connection events, raw button/axis presses, and normalized input streams across Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows, and Web. It also supports controller vibration and rumble effects.
use_when: You are building a game in Flutter that needs multi-platform controller support.
You want consistent normalized gamepad buttons and axes layout across different operating systems.
avoid_when: You only need basic touch and mouse pointer events.
You require complex force feedback features beyond standard dual-motor rumble.
strengths: Supports multiple simultaneous gamepads with auto-connection listening.
Normalized event stream abstracts platform-specific quirks and controller layouts.
weaknesses: Android requires custom MainActivity boilerplate to forward input events.
Vendor and product IDs are null on macOS and iOS.
Linux requires SDL GameController DB mappings for unknown controllers.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding platform-specific handling such as MainActivity boilerplate input dispatching on Android, and C++ desktop support / Windows SDK for Windows targets.
